attacks.claim: Cost math mixes daily and monthly figures. 38M lines/day x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens per day, which at $0.50/1M is ~$1,140 per day (~$34K/month). Output is likewise ~$7/day (~$207/month). The claimed ~$1,150/month is understated ~30x and exceeds the $1,500/month approved budget by more than 20x, so the plan's central budget claim is false.
attacks.evidence: "Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140" and "Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget."

attacks.claim: No spend control: every line is sent unfiltered, with no sampling, per-window token cap, budget alarm or kill switch. Peak day (61M lines, ~1.6x average) and log storms are not costed, and prompt overhead per call is excluded. Spend and latency scale with raw volume exactly during incidents.
attacks.evidence: "forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue"; "Application logs: 38M lines/day average ... (peak day 61M)"; ABSENT: rate cap, max tokens per window, budget alarm

attacks.claim: Both engineers are booked full-time for 6 weeks although the context says on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time. Effective capacity is ~6 eng-weeks against 12 planned, with no contingency. No owner or on-call plan exists for operating the new components after launch.
attacks.evidence: "Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks)." ABSENT: interrupt allowance, post-launch ownership

attacks.claim: Every log line from 30 services goes to an external LLM vendor, but redaction covers only emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs, and was audited for retention policy, not third-party egress. Other PII, secrets and customer data are unaddressed, and there is no minimization analysis. The DPA's coverage of this data flow, the processing region/sub-processors and any customer-notice obligation are not shown.
attacks.evidence: "already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1)"; "Corvid account has zero-retention enabled; data processing addendum signed by Legal (ref DPA-0417)."

attacks.claim: Raw, attacker-influenceable log text is sent to the LLM with a fixed prompt and no isolation from instructions. The output is posted into PagerDuty unvalidated, so injected content can mislead on-call. Nothing says log-tap fails closed if the redaction stage is bypassed or errors, and the handling of the Corvid API credential is unspecified.
attacks.evidence: "sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt"; ABSENT: fail-closed check, credential storage/rotation

attacks.claim: There is no failure-mode design for LLM slowness or outage, or for queue backlog. The PagerDuty comment may carry a stale or missing summary with no age indicator. log-tap on the shared Vector pipeline has no backpressure, isolation, kill switch or rollback, so it could degrade logging for all 30 services. No alerting on summarizer freshness or errors is specified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: timeout/retry/backpressure, staleness display, rollback/disable for log-tap and auto-comments; "Hardening, dashboards, runbook | 2"

attacks.claim: The 47->30 min MTTR target is unsupported. There is no breakdown showing log triage dominates MTTR. The launch gate measures only retrospective summary grades by one commander, with no live pilot, adoption or MTTR criterion. The 'within seconds' promise conflicts with 5-minute batch windows.
attacks.evidence: "Launch gate: >= 70% useful, <= 5% misleading."; "within seconds of a page" vs "every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs"

attacks.claim: Stored summaries and PagerDuty comments are derived from log content but have no retention period or access scoping. Vendor lock-in and exit path are also unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention/access control for summaries; provider abstraction or exit plan
